turns.query: For futures-only CFTC 10-year Treasury note contract 043602 report dates from 2021-2025, inner-join exact same-date Treasury 2- and 10-year yields and SOFR. Define leveraged-money net share as long minus short divided by open interest. Report aligned count/boundaries and select the minimum 10-year-minus-2-year spread, ties earlier, with spread, SOFR and net share. Carry the weekly panel and interpret the relationship and material scope of the curve and positioning measures.

claims.description: The response identifies leveraged-money net share as a CFTC futures-positioning measure rather than cash-Treasury ownership.
If the response causally attributes the curve configuration to same-date positioning, it states that the alignment does not identify causality.

turns.query: Through 2023-12-31, estimate by OLS the normalized long-run relation with 10-year yield dependent on an intercept, 2-year yield and SOFR. On its residual, estimate by OLS an intercept-bearing no-lag ADF regression of residual change on lagged residual; compute the coefficient standard error using residual sum of squares divided by observations minus two. Report count, long-run coefficients, residual n-1 standard deviation, ADF level coefficient and t statistic. Carry the normalized residual forward and interpret what this Engle-Granger-style diagnostic can and cannot license about cointegration.

claims.description: The response treats the residual ADF statistic as a diagnostic for the normalized relation rather than automatic proof of a structural equilibrium.

turns.query: Estimate the conditional rank-one error-correction equation for weekly 10-year-yield change on an intercept, lagged equilibrium error, contemporaneous 2-year-yield change and contemporaneous SOFR change. Report count, coefficients, R-squared and maximum absolute unscaled OLS normal-equation moment. Carry coefficients forward and interpret adjustment sign and contemporaneous-information limits.

claims.description: The response uses the estimated adjustment sign to describe conditional movement toward or away from the fitted relation without claiming causality.

turns.query: Freeze coefficients and evaluate 2024-2025 conditional one-step changes using realized contemporaneous regressors versus a no-change random walk. Report count, both RMSEs and whether ECM is lower. Identify largest absolute actual-minus-predicted error, ties earlier, and report date/error and same-date leveraged-money net share. Explain what using same-day realized inputs does to the standing of this comparison, and how much the matching positioning number can carry.

claims.description: The response identifies realized contemporaneous rate changes as making this an ex-post conditional comparison rather than a deployable one-step forecast.
The response treats the same-date CFTC share as context rather than a causal explanation of the error.

judge_reference.source: The reference aligns weekly CFTC/Treasury/SOFR observations, estimates a normalized rank-one relation and conditional error-correction equation, and evaluates held-out conditional changes without causal or ex-ante claims.
facts: Over 261 weekly observations from 2021-01-05 to 2025-12-30 the deepest inversion is 2023-07-03 at -1.08 percentage points, with SOFR at 5.06 percent and leveraged-money net share at -30.448258 percent of open interest.

The fitted cointegrating relation puts 0.5681 on the two-year yield and 0.0202 on SOFR, with an equilibrium error standard deviation of 0.2069 percentage points. The augmented Dickey-Fuller coefficient on that error is -0.1103 with a t statistic of -3.1434.
The error-correction equation adjusts at -0.0978 per week, roughly a ten-week half-life, and explains 62.3818 percent of weekly changes with a maximum normal moment of zero at the scored precision.
Out of sample over 105 weeks it beats a random walk, 0.0948 against 0.1118 percentage points of root-mean-square error, an improvement of 0.0170, about fifteen percent of the random walk's error.

Its own worst week, 2025-04-08 at 0.2609 percentage points, is more than twice its average error, and leveraged-money net share on that date is -38.307589 percent, more negative than at the deepest inversion.
known_overclaims: Presenting the single cointegrating relation as established; rank is imposed by the question rather than tested by a trace or maximum eigenvalue statistic.
Reading the Dickey-Fuller statistic as a size-correct test; it is computed on a residual from an estimated relation, which changes its distribution.
Treating the weekly leveraged-money aggregate as a directional forecast.
Inferring causality in either direction between positioning and yields.
Presenting a fifteen-percent error improvement as a reliable edge.
